reponse:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reproducing episodic and online test-time adaptation for CLIP under one protocol
PROPOSAL: We re-run eight test-time adaptation methods for CLIP, four episodic (TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT, MTA) and four online (TDA, DMN, DPE, BoostAdapter), from their public code but under a single harness: the same ViT-B/16 and ResNet-50 checkpoints, the same hand-crafted prompt per dataset, the same preprocessing and the same evaluation script, on ImageNet, its four distribution-shift variants and the ten fine-grained datasets. We report top-1 accuracy for each method and for the unadapted model, and we tabulate the difference between our numbers and those printed in each paper.
CONTROLS: The unadapted zero-shot model, each method with the checkpoint and prompt used in its own paper to confirm we can reproduce the printed number before changing conditions, three stream orders for the online methods, and three seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Gains over zero-shot should shrink to under half of the printed gaps once checkpoints and prompts are aligned, and the ranking of the four online methods should change. If printed numbers cannot be reproduced even under original conditions, the discrepancy is in the code rather than in the protocol.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does test-time adaptation compound with prompt learning or cancel it
PROPOSAL: We take CLIP ViT-B/16 checkpoints already tuned at training time with CoOp, CoCoOp, MaPLe and PromptSRC on the 16-shot ImageNet protocol, then apply two episodic methods, TPT and MTA, and two online methods, TDA and DPE, at test time on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-V2 and the fine-grained transfer datasets. For every combination we report accuracy and the change relative to the tuned model alone, and we also report the change relative to the zero-shot model with the same test-time method, which tells us whether the two kinds of gain add, overlap or interfere.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with and without each test-time method, each tuned model without adaptation, a tuned model whose learned prompt is replaced by the hand-crafted prompt to separate the effect of tuning from that of the prompt tokens, and three seeds.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Test-time gains on tuned models should be less than half of the gains on zero-shot CLIP, and on in-domain ImageNet they may become negative for the online methods. Where the hand-crafted prompt substitution restores the test-time gain, the interference comes from the learned prompt rather than from the tuned weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: What test-time adaptation does to calibration, selective prediction and shift detection
PROPOSAL: We measure, beyond accuracy, what adaptation does to the reliability of CLIP ViT-B/16 predictions: expected calibration error, negative log-likelihood, area under the risk-coverage curve for selective prediction, and the AUROC of maximum softmax probability for separating ImageNet from ImageNet-O as an out-of-distribution detection task. Methods are TPT, C-TPT, MTA, TDA and DPE, run on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and the fine-grained datasets. We report every metric before and after adaptation for the same test images, so that each method is characterised by a vector of changes rather than a single accuracy delta.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, temperature scaling of the unadapted model fitted on a held-out split as a calibration-only baseline, each method with its confidence-selection step disabled, and three stream orders for the online methods.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Entropy-minimising methods should lower calibration error on the shifted sets while raising it on in-domain ImageNet, and the risk-coverage area should improve less than accuracy does. If temperature scaling alone matches the calibration changes, the adaptation adds nothing to reliability beyond a confidence rescaling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transferring test-time adaptation methods from CLIP to SigLIP and BLIP-2
PROPOSAL: We port five test-time adaptation methods designed for CLIP, TPT, MTA, TDA, DMN and DPE, to two vision-language models with different training objectives and architectures: SigLIP ViT-B/16, trained with a sigmoid loss, and the image-text matching head of BLIP-2. Each method is re-implemented against the model's own text encoder and similarity function, with hyperparameters re-tuned on a held-out split of ImageNet, and evaluated on ImageNet, its four shift variants and the fine-grained datasets. We report accuracy gains over each unadapted model and the rank correlation between the gains on CLIP and the gains on the other model.
CONTROLS: The CLIP ViT-B/16 results under the same harness, each method with CLIP hyperparameters transferred unchanged to check whether re-tuning matters, the unadapted SigLIP and BLIP-2 models, and three seeds.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Gains on SigLIP should be smaller than on CLIP and the ranking of methods should differ, with the online cache-based methods transferring best. If gains vanish without re-tuning but return with it, the methods are sound but their defaults are tied to CLIP's similarity scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How much of reported progress survives a single checkpoint and prompt
PROPOSAL: We quantify the share of reported test-time adaptation progress attributable to protocol differences by decomposing the gap between the earliest method, TPT, and a recent online method, DPE, into three parts: checkpoint, prompt template and evaluation protocol. We run both methods on CLIP ViT-B/16 under every combination of two checkpoints, three prompt sets and two protocols, on ImageNet and its shift variants, and we fit an additive model to the resulting accuracies to attribute the printed gap to each factor and to the method itself.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model under each combination, both methods with their original settings to reproduce the printed numbers, three stream orders for DPE, and a second recent method, TDA, to check that the attribution is not specific to DPE.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Less than half of the printed gap between TPT and DPE should remain once checkpoint and prompt are equalised, with prompt choice the largest single factor. If the method term dominates instead, recent progress is mostly algorithmic.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of online test-time adaptation under stream order and label shift
PROPOSAL: We test whether online methods for CLIP keep their accuracy when the test stream changes character: we run TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter on ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and the fine-grained datasets under four stream regimes, a random order, a class-sorted order, a stream with a sudden switch between two datasets, and a stream that repeats a small subset many times. We record accuracy over the stream in windows of 500 samples and calculate the variance of windowed accuracy and the worst window for each method. We also measure how fast each method recovers after the dataset switch.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, each episodic method as an order-independent reference, each online method with its cache reset every window, and five random orders to bound the variance expected from sampling alone.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Cache-based methods should lose several points under class-sorted streams and recover slowly after a switch, while episodic methods stay flat. If resetting the cache every window removes the loss, the instability sits in cache contents rather than in the update rule.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial and corruption robustness of CLIP after test-time adaptation
PROPOSAL: We ask whether accuracy-oriented adaptation makes CLIP predictions more fragile. For TPT, MTA, TDA and DPE on ViT-B/16, we evaluate on ImageNet-C at severities one to five and under a transfer attack with PGD crafted on the unadapted model, as well as an adaptive attack that targets the adapted prediction for the episodic methods. We report clean accuracy, corrupted accuracy per severity, attacked accuracy and the gap between clean and attacked accuracy before and after adaptation, on ImageNet and two fine-grained datasets.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, a model with temperature scaling only, each method with its augmentation views replaced by the unaugmented image repeated, and three seeds for the attack.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Adaptation should raise corrupted accuracy at low severity and lower it at severity five, and the attacked gap should widen for the episodic methods whose augmentation selection the attack can target. If the repeated-image variant shows the same fragility, the views are not the entry point.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reporting test-time adaptation gains with confidence intervals across checkpoints
PROPOSAL: Run every public episodic and online method for CLIP under one harness across four checkpoints, ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14 and a ResNet-50, with the same prompts and protocol, and compute for each method and dataset a bootstrap confidence interval over test images together with the standard deviation across checkpoints. Report which pairwise differences between methods remain outside the intervals on ImageNet, its shift variants and the fine-grained datasets, and produce a ranking that only separates methods whose intervals do not overlap on a majority of datasets.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model for each checkpoint, three stream orders for online methods, and a repeat of the whole table with the prompt template changed to test the stability of the ranking.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Most pairwise gaps among recent methods should fall inside the intervals on the majority of datasets, leaving two or three distinguishable tiers. If the ranking changes with the prompt template, the comparison is dominated by prompt choice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does entropy minimisation help on reliability, a metric-by-metric audit of TPT descendants
PROPOSAL: We take the family of episodic methods built on entropy minimisation over augmented views, TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT and RLCF, and audit each on CLIP ViT-B/16 with a panel of reliability metrics: expected calibration error, Brier score, prediction consistency across augmentations, and the fraction of test images whose predicted class flips between the unadapted and adapted model. We run the panel on ImageNet, ImageNet-A and ImageNet-R and on five fine-grained datasets, and we relate the accuracy gain of each method to the flip fraction to see how much of the gain comes from correcting errors versus introducing new ones.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, TPT with the entropy objective replaced by a confidence-maximisation objective, TPT with randomly selected views instead of confidence-selected views, and three seeds.
COST: 110
PREDICTION: Flip fractions should exceed the net accuracy gain by a factor of three or more, meaning methods swap many predictions to gain a few. If the random-view variant matches the confidence-selected one, the selection step is not what drives the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Replaying the adaptation literature in order to measure cumulative progress
PROPOSAL: We arrange ten test-time adaptation methods for CLIP in order of their appearance, from TPT to the most recent online method, and run each under the same harness on ViT-B/16 with the same prompts on ImageNet, its shift variants and the fine-grained datasets. We then plot the accuracy of each method against its position in the sequence and fit a piecewise-linear trend, which gives the cumulative gain over the first method and the gain of each method over its immediate predecessor under equal conditions. We repeat the plot for the gains each paper printed to compare the two trends.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model as the origin of both curves, each method also run with its own paper's checkpoint and prompt, and three stream orders for the online methods.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The printed trend should rise steadily while the equal-conditions trend should flatten after the first two online methods. If the two trends agree, protocol variation has not contributed to the reported progress.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reproducing Test-Time Adaptation for CLIP Under One Shared Evaluation Protocol
PROPOSAL: Re-run six episodic and online adaptation methods, including entropy-based prompt tuning, cache-based adaptation and confidence-weighted ensembling, on CLIP ViT-B/16 with one released checkpoint, one shared set of prompt templates and one data order, over ImageNet, its four natural-shift variants and ten fine-grained datasets. Record top-1 accuracy for each method and each dataset, and the improvement over the unadapted model with a paired bootstrap interval, so that the gains attributable to each algorithm are separated from checkpoint and prompt differences.
CONTROLS: Compare every method against the unadapted CLIP run under the same checkpoint and the same prompts. Compare every method with its reported number from the original paper, to see how far the reported figures shift. Compare each online method with its episodic counterpart under the same data order. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The improvement over the unadapted model should be smaller than the reported figures for most methods, and the ranking of recent against early methods should narrow. The conclusion fails if the gaps to the reported figures stay within the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Adaptation for CLIP Judged Against Training-Time Prompt Learning
PROPOSAL: Re-run six episodic and online adaptation methods, including entropy-based prompt tuning, cache-based adaptation and confidence-weighted ensembling, on CLIP ViT-B/16 using each method's own released checkpoint and preferred prompt templates, over ImageNet, its four natural-shift variants and ten fine-grained datasets. Record top-1 accuracy for each method and each dataset, and the improvement over a prompt-learned model trained on sixteen labelled shots per class, with a paired bootstrap interval for each difference.
CONTROLS: Compare every method against a few-shot prompt-learned CLIP run under the same checkpoint and the same prompts. Compare every method with its larger ViT-L/14 variant from the original paper, to see how far the larger figures shift. Compare each online method with a labelled fine-tuning counterpart under the same data order. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The improvement over the prompt-learned model should be smaller than the reported figures for most methods, and the ranking of recent against early methods should narrow. The conclusion fails if the gaps to the larger figures stay within the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Do Test-Time Gains Survive a Change of Checkpoint and Prompt Template?
PROPOSAL: Evaluate four representative adaptation methods on three CLIP checkpoints, namely the OpenAI release, a LAION-trained release and a DataComp-trained release at ViT-B/16, using eight prompt template sets that range from a single class-name template to an ensemble of eighty hand-written ones. Measure top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and five fine-grained datasets, then fit a mixed-effects model with method, checkpoint and template as factors to estimate how much of each reported gain depends on the choice of checkpoint and template.
CONTROLS: Vary the checkpoint while the prompt template set is held fixed. Compare each method with the unadapted model that uses the same checkpoint and template. Vary the prompt template set while the checkpoint is held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Reported gains should shrink by a third or more with the ensembled templates, and the ranking of methods should change across checkpoints. The study fails to show a dependence if the mixed-effects interaction terms stay inside their intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Gains Under Changes of Image Scale and View Counts
PROPOSAL: Evaluate four representative adaptation methods on one CLIP checkpoint, namely the OpenAI release at ViT-B/16, using one template set, with augmented-view counts per test image ranging from eight to sixty-four and image scales from 224 to 336 pixels. Measure top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and five fine-grained datasets, then fit a mixed-effects model with method, image scale and view count as factors to estimate how much of each gain depends on these evaluation details.
CONTROLS: Vary the image scale while the view count is held fixed. Compare each method with the unadapted model that uses the same image scale and view count. Vary the view count while the image scale is held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Reported gains should shrink by a third or more with larger view counts, and the ranking of methods should change across image scales. The study fails to show a dependence if the mixed-effects interaction terms stay inside their intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does Adaptation Help Models That Were Already Tuned? Test-Time Methods on Prompt-Learned CLIP
PROPOSAL: Take CLIP ViT-B/16 checkpoints tuned with CoOp, MaPLe and PromptSRC on ImageNet with sixteen labelled shots per class, then apply three adaptation methods at test time, one episodic and two online, on ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch as natural shifts. Report top-1 accuracy of each tuned model with and without adaptation, and the shared improvement, to learn how adaptation complements or conflicts with training-time tuning.
CONTROLS: Compare each adaptation method on the tuned checkpoint against the same tuned checkpoint without adaptation. Compare each adaptation method on the tuned checkpoint with the same method on the untuned CLIP, under the same prompts. Compare the three tuning recipes with the same adaptation method held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Gains on tuned checkpoints should be smaller than on untuned CLIP, and one tuning recipe may conflict with cache-based adaptation. The claim fails if the improvement is the same on every checkpoint.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Methods on Zero-Shot CLIP With Clean In-Distribution Test Data
PROPOSAL: Take CLIP ViT-B/16 checkpoints used zero-shot with ensembled prompts, then apply three adaptation methods at test time, one episodic and two online, on the ImageNet validation split and its ten-percent and fifty-percent subsets as in-distribution data. Report top-1 accuracy of each model with and without adaptation, and the shared improvement, to learn how the methods behave on data drawn from the same distribution as the pretraining benchmark.
CONTROLS: Compare each adaptation method on the zero-shot checkpoint against the same zero-shot checkpoint without adaptation. Compare each adaptation method on the validation split with the same method on its subsets, under the same prompts. Compare the three data fractions with the same adaptation method held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Gains on the validation split should be smaller than on shifted data, and one fraction may conflict with cache-based adaptation. The claim fails if the improvement is the same on every fraction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration, Selective Accuracy and Robustness After Test-Time Adaptation of CLIP
PROPOSAL: For eight adaptation methods on CLIP ViT-B/16, measure beyond top-1 accuracy: expected calibration error, selective accuracy at several coverage levels, out-of-distribution detection with maximum softmax score, and accuracy on ImageNet-C at five corruption severities. Run on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ten fine-grained datasets, and summarise with rank correlations that show whether the methods improving accuracy most also degrade calibration or robustness, with intervals from a bootstrap over images.
CONTROLS: Measure calibration error and detection quality for each method and for the unadapted model on identical images. Compare accuracy gains with changes in calibration for the same methods, under the same prompts. Compare corrupted and clean inputs with the adaptation held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Accuracy-driven entropy minimisation should raise calibration error on shifted data, and the methods with the largest gains should show the largest degradation. The claim fails if calibration error changes by less than the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Computational Cost and Footprint of Test-Time Adaptation Methods for CLIP
PROPOSAL: Profile eight adaptation methods applied to CLIP ViT-B/16 on engineering terms beyond accuracy alone: peak footprint, wall-clock time per image, count of updated parameters, and forward passes needed under five augmentation counts. Use ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ten fine-grained datasets, and summarise with rank correlations showing whether the methods improving accuracy most also consume more time or footprint, with intervals from a bootstrap over images.
CONTROLS: Measure runtime and footprint for each method and for the unadapted model on identical images. Compare accuracy gains with changes in runtime for the same methods, under the same prompts. Compare large and small inputs with the adaptation held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Accuracy-driven entropy minimisation should raise runtime on shifted data, and the methods with the largest gains should show the largest cost. The claim fails if runtime changes by less than the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Beyond CLIP: Do Test-Time Gains Transfer to Other Vision-Language Architectures?
PROPOSAL: Apply three adaptation methods, one episodic and two online, to CLIP ViT-L/14, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP and a BLIP-based image-text model, using one prompt template set and one data order, across ImageNet, its four variants and ten fine-grained datasets. For each architecture record the gain over the unadapted model, together with the gain a method delivers on CLIP ViT-B/16 as the reference, and check whether rankings of methods stay the same when the architecture changes.
CONTROLS: Compare each method on each architecture against the unadapted version of that architecture. Compare each method on the other architectures with the same method on the CLIP reference. Compare the rankings across architectures with the dataset held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Gains should be smaller on the architectures trained with sigmoid or larger-scale objectives, and at least one method should rank differently. The claim fails if rankings are the same on every architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling Study of Test-Time Gains Across CLIP Checkpoint Scale
PROPOSAL: Run one episodic method and two online methods on the small, base and large CLIP checkpoints and a large checkpoint fed bigger inputs, holding the template set and data order common, over ImageNet, four variants of it and ten fine-grained collections. At each scale compute the gain relative to the unadapted model, together with the gain obtained on CLIP ViT-B/16 as the reference, and check whether method rankings stay the same when scale changes.
CONTROLS: Compare each method on each scale against the unadapted version of that scale. Compare each method on the other scales with the same method on the CLIP reference. Compare the rankings across scales with the dataset held fixed. Repeat the stream order over three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Gains should be smaller on the larger-scale checkpoints, and at least one method should rank differently. The claim fails if rankings are the same at every scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attributing the printed gap between TPT and DPE to checkpoint, prompt and protocol
PROPOSAL: We run TPT and DPE on CLIP ViT-B/16 under every combination of two checkpoints, three prompt sets and two evaluation protocols on ImageNet and its shift variants, fit an additive model to the accuracies with each cell run on the full validation set, and read off how much of the printed gap each factor explains and how much is left for the method itself.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model under each combination, both methods at their original settings to reproduce the printed numbers, TDA as a second recent method, bootstrap intervals over images, three stream orders, three seeds.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Prompt choice should be the largest factor and under half of the printed gap should remain. It fails if the method term dominates, in which case progress is algorithmic.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A meta-analysis of printed test-time adaptation results across papers
PROPOSAL: We collect the accuracy tables printed in twenty-five papers on test-time adaptation for CLIP, record for each entry the checkpoint, prompt template, evaluation protocol and dataset, and fit a mixed-effects regression of printed accuracy on these covariates with a random effect per paper, so that each method's coefficient is adjusted for them. We then rank methods by their adjusted coefficient on ImageNet and its shift variants and compare the adjusted ranking with the raw ranking.
CONTROLS: The regression refitted without the paper random effect, with the covariates permuted across entries, and with the entries restricted to papers that report all four covariates.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: The adjusted ranking should differ from the raw one for about a third of the methods, with prompt template the strongest covariate. It fails if the permuted fit gives the same coefficients, meaning the covariates carry no information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Testing adaptation on three vision-language families with training-time tuning crossed in
PROPOSAL: We port TPT, MTA, TDA and DPE to SigLIP ViT-B/16 and to BLIP-2's image-text matching head, each re-implemented against the model's own similarity function with hyperparameters re-tuned on a held-out ImageNet split, and we cross this with training-time tuning by also running each method on CoOp- and MaPLe-tuned versions of CLIP and SigLIP, so that both the model axis and the tuning axis are covered in one table on ImageNet, its shift variants and the fine-grained datasets.
CONTROLS: CLIP ViT-B/16 under the same harness, each unadapted and each tuned model alone, CLIP hyperparameters carried over unchanged, three stream orders, and three seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gains should shrink on SigLIP and shrink further on tuned models, with online methods transferring best. It fails if re-tuned hyperparameters restore CLIP-level gains everywhere, meaning only the defaults were tied to CLIP.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How test-time adaptation gains scale with CLIP model size
PROPOSAL: We run TPT, MTA, TDA and DPE on four CLIP checkpoints of increasing size, ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14 and ViT-H/14, under one harness on ImageNet, its shift variants and the fine-grained datasets, and we fit the gain of each method against the zero-shot accuracy of the checkpoint to see whether adaptation helps less as the base model improves, reporting the slope per method and per dataset family.
CONTROLS: Each unadapted checkpoint, each method with hyperparameters re-tuned per checkpoint against the ViT-B/16 defaults carried over, three stream orders, and three seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gains should fall with zero-shot accuracy for the episodic methods and stay flat for the online ones. It fails if re-tuning per checkpoint changes the slopes, meaning the trend reflects defaults rather than scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does adaptation trade reliability for accuracy across the full method set
PROPOSAL: We run ten episodic and online methods on CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 across ImageNet, its shift variants, ImageNet-C at five severities and the fine-grained datasets, and for each we record accuracy together with calibration error, selective risk, out-of-distribution AUROC against ImageNet-O, consistency under stream order and accuracy under a transfer PGD attack, before and after adaptation on the same images, so that every change is attributable to the adaptation step.
CONTROLS: The unadapted models, temperature scaling as a calibration-only comparison, each method with confidence selection disabled, each method with its augmentation views replaced by the plain image repeated, five stream orders, three attack seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Methods with the largest accuracy gains should show the largest calibration and attack degradation. It fails if the two are uncorrelated across methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An uncertainty-weighted cache for online adaptation of CLIP
PROPOSAL: We propose an online method in which each cached test feature is weighted by the agreement between its augmented views, so that entries whose predictions vary across views contribute less to the class prototypes, and we combine the weighted prototypes with the zero-shot logits through a learned mixing coefficient updated by entropy minimisation. We run it on CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 on ImageNet, its shift variants, ImageNet-C at five severities and the fine-grained datasets, and we report accuracy against TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter under one harness.
CONTROLS: The unadapted models, the cache with uniform weights, the mixing coefficient fixed, five stream orders, three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The weighted cache should beat DPE by about one point on the shifted sets. It fails if uniform weights do as well.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of online adaptation under adversarial stream orders
PROPOSAL: We run TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter on CLIP ViT-B/16 over ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and the fine-grained datasets under random, class-sorted, dataset-switching and repeated-subset streams, record accuracy in windows of 500 samples, and report windowed variance, worst window and recovery time after a switch, so that stability is measured directly rather than inferred from average accuracy.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, episodic TPT and MTA as order-independent references, each online method with its cache reset per window, five random orders, three seeds.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Cache methods should lose several points under sorted streams and recover slowly after a switch. It fails if cache resets remove the loss, placing the instability in cache contents.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency and memory profile of test-time adaptation methods for deployment
PROPOSAL: We profile TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT, MTA, TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter on CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14, measuring per-image latency, peak memory, number of forward and backward passes, and cache growth over a stream of ImageNet and ImageNet-R, at two batch sizes, and we plot each method's accuracy against its latency to find the methods on the accuracy-latency frontier for each dataset.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model as the origin of the frontier, each method with fewer augmentation views, the online caches capped at two sizes, five runs per measurement, three seeds.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The online methods should sit on the frontier below ten times the unadapted latency while the episodic methods fall off it. It fails if accuracy with fewer views matches the full set, in which case the frontier collapses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Corruption and attack robustness of CLIP before and after adaptation
PROPOSAL: We evaluate TPT, MTA, TDA and DPE on CLIP ViT-B/16 over ImageNet-C at severities one to five and under a transfer PGD attack crafted on the unadapted model plus an adaptive attack aimed at the adapted prediction for the episodic methods, on ImageNet and two fine-grained datasets, with attacks run on a fixed subset of one thousand images per dataset, reporting clean, corrupted and attacked accuracy and the clean-to-attacked gap before and after adaptation.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, temperature scaling only, each method with views replaced by the plain image repeated, attack strength at two levels, bootstrap intervals over images, three attack seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Adaptation should help at low severity and hurt at severity five, and the attacked gap should widen for episodic methods. It fails if the repeated-image variant is equally fragile.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt template sensitivity of zero-shot CLIP across checkpoints and datasets
PROPOSAL: We measure how much zero-shot accuracy of CLIP moves with the prompt template alone, running ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 with eighty hand-written templates, the single default template and the ensemble of all templates, on ImageNet, its shift variants and the fine-grained datasets, and we report for each dataset the spread between the best and worst template, the gain of the ensemble over the default, and the correlation of template quality across checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Templates with the class name removed as a floor, templates with words shuffled, the ensemble restricted to ten random templates, three random template subsets.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The spread between templates should exceed the gains most adaptation papers print, and template quality should correlate across checkpoints. It fails if the shuffled templates match the default, meaning the text encoder ignores word order.
